mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of over 10% in the same month indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST < previous month - 10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 6% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% from the previous month, sustained for two consecutive months, signals contraction in manufacturing output and input demand, which depresses earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month - 1% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not negative in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and a fall in payroll employment (PAYEMS) by more than 100,000 in the same month signals accelerating job losses, which reduces consumer spending and corporate revenues, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises AND PAYEMS falls by >100,000 in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) of more than 1% for three consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate sales and profit growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < previous month - 1% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month increase in the federal funds rate of more than 0.75 percentage points, combined with a concurrent rise in CPIAUCSL above 3%, signals aggressive monetary tightening and accelerating inflation, which increases interest rates and reduces equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS change > 0.75% AND CPIAUCSL > previous month + 3%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized GDP growth rate (GDPC1) below 1% for four consecutive quarters signals economic stagnation, which erodes corporate earnings and investor confidence, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of other conditions.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of quarters with GDPC1 < 1% annualized for four straight quarters.
